checks.requirement: C++23, Qt discovery, target/moc/QML/qrc and Review/production closure
checks.evidence: YalahooScene owns RenderQuality with QObject/moc and QtGui; app registers foreign type, aliases three new scene components, embeds four SSAO shaders, the shadow diagnostic and six fixed textures. The source manifest is also embedded. Independent Review image audit links QtGui and QtQuick for the public backend enum, app Review CLI/source remains conditional. Shared targets keep explicit C++23 and common latest-Kit discovery; no OS-specific calls or new link library. Release Review and production regressions plus qmllint execute on Windows. Platform.cmake applies /W4, NOMINMAX, WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN only on WIN32; APPLE and UNIX use warning flags. App WIN32_EXECUTABLE, APPLE bundle identity and UNIX origin-relative RPATH remain separate branches; occlusion-audit is an ordinary console executable on all three. The existing asset helper links dwrite only inside WIN32. main selects D3D11 only for Q_OS_WIN, Metal for Q_OS_MACOS and OpenGL for Q_OS_LINUX. New shaders contain no platform-only intrinsic, no forced backend and no disabled product branch.
checks.limitations: Target compiler/linker not run on this platform. Full platform packaging remains R31/R32.

checks.requirement: Resource identity, float endian, logical dimensions, size/device limits
checks.evidence: FixedTextureData accepts only named 16/32/64 kernel/noise assets via qrc, validates exact dimensions and byte count, swaps every float word on big-endian. Kernel rows are count-by-1, noise 4-by-4, repeated nearest sampling. RenderQuality separates authored values from bounded targets; resize rejects nonfinite/nonpositive inputs and never mutates preferences. Main target explicit dimensions and geometry/AO target sizes share the same quality object; screen DPR changes trigger measurement. Product uses conservative 4096 bound until backend reports a device limit. No current-directory/private-library paths are introduced.
checks.limitations: Native DPR/runtime sourceItem texture direction needs target testing. Device-specific raw depth format is Qt-owned and not exposed by public API.

checks.requirement: Opaque glass override, view normals, scalar depth reconstruction and multipass buffers
checks.evidence: Separate override includes all case surfaces and full paper, preserving Three MeshNormalMaterial semantics. Qt signed world normals are transformed by VIEW_MATRIX once. Hardware depth [0,1] is converted to linear distance and carried as RGB24 exact bytes in an independent opaque-alpha geometry prepass, alongside the normal prepass. This survives the public View3D texture provider color quantization; scalar inverse uses source vertical FOV/aspect and FRAMEBUFFER_Y_UP, avoiding backend clip-range duplication. TBN, scalar noise, strict distance interval, 5x5 blur and .22 multiplier match the source. Every Pass writes a distinct Buffer; final pass samples original color and named AO/blur buffers with Qt-generated bindings. Raw channels bypass sRGB; shaded paper consumes shadow-only hook while preserving original custom radiometry. SPIR-V, desktop/ES GLSL, HLSL, MSL wrappers compile with the same latest Kit. Windows runtime also compiles generated shaders, proves nonwhite diagnostic AO and actual shadow on/off pixels. Unshaded shell reception and exact public shadow projection/filter limitations are concretely assigned to R10, output conversion to R09B.
checks.limitations: MSL/GLSL generation is static evidence, not target GPU execution. Public shadow fitting/bias/filter and sourceItem precision require target GPU validation; known visual limitations remain explicit future-round inputs.

checks.requirement: Quality changes, destruction and media/state isolation
checks.evidence: RenderQuality is a value-owning SceneAdapter member, independent from lighting, motion and media. Preset changes update only quality signals and render resources; unit test preserves frame revision, pose, detail and lighting identity across all four presets. Performance disables geometry Loader unless a geometry probe needs it; restoring recreates only the render prepass. Objects and TextureData remain owned by the QML tree, with sourceItem lifetime handled by Qt. No new thread/network/media source or device operation; existing single-clock/hidden-window behavior and QtMultimedia objects remain unchanged. Production shading runtime exercises the same QML effects without Review code.
checks.limitations: Long-duration resource/performance convergence belongs to R28. No new media operation is introduced in R09.

checks.requirement: Frozen provenance, genuine Windows GPU evidence and limitations
checks.evidence: Source comes from git archive/show at the frozen commit; locked dependency hashes and all six texture byte hashes are verified. Browser harness uses repository-contained isolated profile, denies nonlocal requests and anonymous covers. Fixtures distinguish 80 production states, 6 algorithm stress states and 2 shadow receivers; no diagnostic overrides are saved as production settings. Windows actual images, DPR=1, D3D11, rendered frames, dimensions, projection, source parameters, raw depth/normal and nonwhite AO/shadow pixels are checked. Four material ROIs of single-case states have independent numeric gates; background color-output and overlap limitations retain full metrics/images and explicit owner rounds. Reports do not claim these limitations are solved or infer target runtime from generated shader variants. Raw AO/blur full-image MAE must remain below .05/255, and a source-white far-plane background stays white. The audit checks the platform-specific public backend enum (D3D11/Metal/OpenGL), matching main rather than imposing D3D11 on non-Windows.
checks.limitations: This platform's build/GPU/GUI/audio has not been executed. R10 and R09B must consume the named residual inputs before full visual acceptance.
